children: Tesla, Inc. (NASDAQ:TSLA) is pressing forward on AI and autonomy—Nevada approved up to 5,000 robo‑taxis, Cybercab and Robotaxi work continues, Semi and Optimus are being scaled—while energy/storage, solar shifts and mixed margins temper investor enthusiasm amid volatile stock moves.
Previous Week Recap
Nevada Approves 5,000 Robo-taxis
: Nevada approved Tesla to deploy up to 5,000 robo-taxis in 12 months. Approval follows Tesla’s Austin robotaxi launch and coincided with intraday TSLA share swings of about 2.5–3.8%.
Tesla Energy Storage 13.5 GWh
: Tesla (TSLA) deployed 13.5 GWh of energy storage in Q2, up 53% sequentially. Energy gross margin fell to 20.4% from 39.5% after a $240M warranty adjustment and weaker prices.
Tesla Plans Semi Self-Driving Rollout
: Tesla (TSLA) plans self-driving Tesla Semi by late 2026–early 2027, aims to scale Semi production next year, and will inaugurate its Nevada Semi factory on Sept. 24.
Cybertruck Deliveries Modest, Share Underwhelming

: Tesla (TSLA) reports modest Cybertruck deliveries, production well below Gigafactory Texas capacity; Cybertruck counted in "Other Models" and represents a small share of recent quarterly deliveries.
Cybercab Unveiling Planned September 3
: Tesla (TSLA) will unveil the production Cybercab on September 3 in Austin. Designed for autonomous ride‑hailing, it lacks steering and pedals and will use Tesla's Full Self‑Driving software.
Tesla Denies FSD Wind‑Down In China
: Tesla (TSLA) denied reports it’s winding down FSD in China, confirmed its Shanghai data center is active, FSD work is ongoing, and hiring for China self‑driving roles continues.
Solar Roof Sold Out, Standard Panels Next
: Tesla (TSLA) stopped selling Solar Roof tiles and will sell standard solar panels instead, shifting its solar hardware offering to conventional panels for customer installations.
Optimus Gen 3 Mass Production Target
: Tesla (TSLA) advances Optimus Gen 3 for mass production, targeting start before end of 2026. Fremont plant prepped for first large-scale line with eventual 1 million robots/year capacity.
High P/E, AI Hype Not Earnings Catalyst
: TSLA trades at a very high P/E, valuing future AI and self‑driving gains over current earnings; hype around the flying Roadster seen as spectacle, not a material catalyst for results.
FSD/Robotaxi Progress Amid Demand Signals
: Tesla (TSLA) shows progress on Full Self-Driving and Robotaxi projects and signs of improving vehicle demand; upcoming PCE data may affect investor pricing of Tesla’s future earnings.
